At the district level, we can take Sydney’s business centers as an example of a area that developed its pre-colonial landscape until it became a two-tiered city. Initially, the maximum height was 45 meters, and later came the very tall towers we see today. At a much smaller scale, the same can happen in Sydney’s urban centers around transportation hubs. The inner suburbs also need to evolve, with a trend toward more affordable housing at heights below tree tops in key areas. Of course, the new housing development must be well-designed and include trees, parks, gardens, and other essential infrastructure.

Our planning system also needs to be adapted so that planners in suburban areas—who seem less willing to change—are not the only ones determining the future shape of their suburbs. One way forward could be to have an independent decision-making body that safeguards quality designs, provided they remain below tree tops, include family homes, spacious balconies and community gardens, and also have a pleasant appearance. This could be the role for the current architect in New South Wales’ government, working within carefully developed compliance guidelines.

Over the past decade, our lives have changed thanks to technology; many people now work from home, and Sydney now has an impressive network of metros and light trains. The power to buy online has also changed the way we shop, and friends and family seem closer thanks to smartphone communication. All these adaptations from one system to another can also occur in existing buildings in our environment, through planning focused on adaptive reuse rather than prioritizing the preservation of heritage.

Chris Johnson is a former government architect in New South Wales (1995–2005) and executive director of the New South Wales Planning Department (2005–2009). He was executive director of Urban Taskforce Australia from 2011 to 2019.
A final push for women's equality
Last year, the World Economic Forum predicted that it would take five generations to achieve gender equality in all nations. Now, the World Bank wants to accelerate that timeline quickly.

The international financial institution is ready to launch a strategy aimed at significantly promoting the economic rights and opportunities of girls and women by 2030. The plan focuses on improving inclusion and resilience through access to financing, technological innovation, and changes in laws and public policies.

“Recent studies show that both social norms and mindsets can change; for example, involving men and children can encourage their support and acceptance of gender equality,” a draft consultation document states. “Positive gender outcomes can be accelerated and expanded through a better understanding of how social norms and mindsets shape expectations, priorities, and daily practices.”

Mindset changes are more difficult to quantify than bank loans for rural women or girls' schooling. Nevertheless, there is ample evidence that female action can move mountains. In Iran, for example, women have led the greatest threat to the Islamic government in 40 years by simply refusing to comply with laws that require them to cover their hair. In some of the 130 countries with minimum quotas for female representation in government, such as India, male resistance to female voting and political activism has decreased.

In some rural communities in Africa, civil society organizations are replacing a harmful initiation ritual with health education. One of these programs helped Kamanda Timayio, a leader of the Masai village of Maparasha (Kenya), change his opinion on female genital mutilation. He told Le Monde that he had “left behind ignorance” and would abandon this practice.

The World Bank cites other examples. From 1970 to 2022, Bangladesh quadrupled female literacy rates and doubled women’s participation in the active labor force. Its gross domestic product more than tripled. The change gained momentum on its own. The recruitment of salaried women as teachers and health workers within their own communities boosted confidence and made women’s mobility and work more socially acceptable.

The bank’s plan aims to focus on norms and institutions that may still require generational changes. Rwanda took over two decades to establish itself as a model for land reform that promotes women’s economic empowerment: “No one benefits if women are suppressed,” said Rwanda’s president, Paul Kagame, defending the land reform in 2015. “We need to change mindsets, not just laws.”
The World Bank hopes to spread that message.

Washington’s prison system is facing a mortality crisis. This is a uncomfortable but inevitable reality that we face as co-chairs of a legislative working group tasked with studying our prison system and recommending changes to make prisons safer. Although we come from different fields—prison administration, civil rights advocacy, and personal prison experience—we all agree that there should be independent oversight of Washington’s prisons.

More than 130,000 people were placed in a prison in Washington in 2022, yet there is a surprising lack of information about what happens once they arrive there. Washington lacks a state office to monitor prisons and provide data to the public. Some of the only available data refer to deaths in custody.

What we have discovered shows that immediate action is necessary. Even considering the increase in the population of Washington, the death rate in its prisons nearly tripled between 2000 and 2019 (a 16-fold increase compared to the national average). Outperforming other states, Washington currently has the fourth-highest prison mortality rate in the country. This cannot continue.

Reversing the rising mortality rate in prisons and addressing many other problems faced by our prisons may require difficult political decisions. However `' an independent oversight of prisons is a crucial first step toward a safer and more humane prison system. Independent oversight is a proven method to improve transparency and accountability both in Washington and across the country. According to our calculations, at least 25 states have state offices responsible for prison oversight, and all of them have a lower death rate than Washington.

In our case, Washington hasoulli recently established or expanded independent oversight in prisons, police, schools, and other state entities. Prisons are the notable exception to this oversight among institutions responsible for the health and safety of tens of thousands of people.

An independent prison oversight office can monitor conditions, hold meetings with employees and inmates, report on situations witnessed firsthand, and even convey concerns before injuries occur. A prison oversight office can also collect data and provide information, helping administrators, lawmakers, and the public understand our prison system and promote solutions to prison mortality and other related issues based on this data.

Oversight is not only focused on the benefit of inmates. Our working group identified that an oversight office can collaborate with overwhelmed prison systems to facilitate much-needed assistance and recommendations, including smart policies to promote employee safety and reduce recidivism.

From 1981 to 1987, Washington state briefly had a state prison oversight office, which was praised by the U.S. Justice Department as a model for the country's systems. How to know if you're flying on a Boeing 737 MAX

For most travelers, the aircraft model is not a decisive factor when booking a flight. However, with most Boeing 737 MAX 9 aircraft immobilized across the country after the fuselage collapse of Alaska Airlines on January 6th, some future passengers may want to know what type of aircraft they will use and which models are the safest. The first question is fairly easy to answer; the second is a bit more complicated.

The aircraft type is usually specified in the flight booking information. On Google Flights, it is included in flight details when a ticket page is expanded, and is typically listed on individual airline pages. If, for some reason, the aircraft type is not displayed on Google Flights or the booking page, some sites like Expert Flyer and Seat Guru collect information about the flights, such as seat maps and aircraft types.

Determining the safest aircraft models is not so simple. The National Transportation Safety Board has complete databases with information on accidents and incidents. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) also provides preliminary reports on accidents and incidents over the past 10 days, including the aircraft manufacturer involved, on its Aviation Safety Analysis and Information Exchange page.

The FAA also provides a link to another useful resource: the Boeing Global Statistical Summary of Jet Airplane Accidents from 1959 to 2022. This summary evaluates safety based on aircraft type, with a breakdown of accidents by model. According to the report published in September 2023,老实 787 and Airbus A350 are the aircraft models with the fewest total hull losses—those accidents in which the aircraft is destroyed without any possibility of repair. There are a few other models in the report that never experienced a hull loss, such as the two-story Airbus A380,))* but those models had fewer than 1 million takeoffs at the time of the report's publication.

The report also includes a comparison of hull loss rates per million flights, taking into account that some models are more common or have been in service for longer than others. The Airbus A310 breakthrough in 1983 has the highest hull loss rate at 2.53 per million flights among models still in service as passenger aircraft. The Airbus 320 family, including the A321 and A319neo, has the lowest rate at 0.11. The婆婆 Boeing 737 MAX line, in service since 2017, has a rate of 1.48.

It is important to note that, although these indices are per million departures, some aircraft models in the report, such as the Boeing 727 presented in 1964, have existed for decades, and therefore have had more time to accumulate accidents compared to others.

Perry Cooper, the media representative for the Seattle Port, who oversees the Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, said in an email that there are many factors that lead to accidents, ranging from equipment errors to human mistakes. So, while it’s quite simple to determine the type of plane you’ll be flying on, it’s more complicated to understand what that means from a safety perspective.

Although you can compare aircraft models based on available information, the FAA recommends avoiding trying to compare airlines based on their accident reports. According to a report cited by the administration, “there is currently no evidence in accident data that allows for classifying individual airlines based on their safety records.”

According to the FAA, although there arence significant differences in airlines’ safety records at specific times, this is mostly due to the “rare but catastrophic nature of an air accident”. These apparent differences between airlines eventually even out over time. The FAA rejected our request for comments.
